events.title: NW-local proof-carrying structural selector class refuted on frozen hard family
events.hypothesis: A universal polynomial Akinator may be obtained by selecting only B2 macros whose transitive root support stays inside one NW neighborhood, provided the candidates and progress certificates are polynomially enumerable/checkable.
formal_statement: On the frozen existential NW-parity hard family, every NW-neighborhood-local B2/ER3 refutation has superpolynomial size and superpolynomial extension count in actual encoded input length.
Therefore a selector restricted to NW-local B2 macros cannot both terminate on every sufficiently large hard-family member and keep total work/extension count bounded by N^c for one fixed c.
Such a selector must return UNKNOWN, exceed polynomial resources, or emit a cross-neighborhood macro.
events.external_basis: Dmitry Sokolov, Pseudorandom Generators, Resolution and Heavy Width, CCC 2022.
events.next_gap: Permit cross-neighborhood macros and quantify the minimum structural complexity a polynomial selector vocabulary must support.

events.title: Low width-depth structural vocabulary refuted; robust survival becomes next certificate resource
formal_statement: For any polynomial-size B2/ER3 escape on the frozen NW hard-family transfer, negative-frontier width b and inversion depth d must obey (d+1)*log(b+2)=Omega(log N).
Hence any selector class whose successful runs guarantee b<=B(N), d<=D(N) with (D(N)+1)*log(B(N)+2)=o(log N) cannot be a universal polynomial escape on that family.
Constant b requires d=Omega(log N); constant d requires b=N^Omega(1); polylogarithmic b requires d=Omega(log N/log log N).

However large original b,d is not itself a valid progress certificate: the F3D.D0 abstract counterfamily has arbitrarily large pre-restriction b,d but a one-root-bit restriction collapses every crossing macro to a constant.
required_certificate_components: restriction-robust semantic survival under an exact source-matched restriction relation/distribution
events.next_gap: Build or refute a polynomially discoverable robust structural progress certificate without exact coNP-hard semantic usefulness and without exponential schema backtracking.

events.title: Structural-selector finite probe failed on premature asymptotic dominance assertion
diagnosis: The fixture incorrectly demanded N^(1/4) > (log_2 N)^2 already for small N=2^k with k in 8..20.
For those finite values the inequality can be reversed even though N^(1/4) eventually dominates (log N)^2.
This is a finite-fixture bug, not evidence against the F3 asymptotic tradeoff.
events.repair_rule: Move only this dominance witness to an explicitly verified sufficiently-large-k regime; keep the analytical theorem independent of the finite replay.
events.next_gap: Repair fixture, rerun independently, preserve this failed receipt permanently.

active_front.name: AKINATOR-RSPC
active_front.current_exact_question: Can a deterministic polynomial selector find a cross-neighborhood B2 macro with a polynomially checkable certificate of restriction-robust structural survival and certified global progress, for every nonterminal CNF/proof state?
active_front.adversarial_question: Can a polynomial-size macro family pass every proposed cheap structural certificate while collapsing under the exact source-matched restriction relation?
forbidden_shortcuts: finite replay promoted to asymptotic theorem
